results.rationale: To set up a tangent equation, the learner builds y = m(x − x0) + y0 from the derivative value and the point. That is the point-slope competence of ae772695-d55e-4cc5-81bc-6605272759b4, and nothing secured today provides it: the secured goals are only J5–J7 arithmetic plus the E-phase entry to the derivative. ae772695 is the only goal in the listings that develops it; its J10 twin b43a1e45-f05c-4d78-8453-f6fa677dc24c applies in only 2 states, and the E siblings are not narrower.
results.concerns: J8 → E points backwards, and both goals apply in all 16 states. Candidate 13 proposes the same edge for the sibling f042385e, which shows how much the tangent goals in the E cluster 'Tangenten, Normalen und Steigungswinkel untersuchen' overlap.

results.rationale: Computing the slope angle means α = arctan(m): the learner determines an angle from the tangent ratio in the slope triangle. 71a483ba-9680-4654-bb5e-5ab5427f0919 is the only goal in the listings that develops this, and nothing secured for the goal provides it. The sibling 6aed5be9 is a parallel E goal rather than an earlier step, and it does not secure trigonometry itself.
results.concerns: J9 → E points backwards, all 16 states. The edge brings 13 Sek I geometry goals (Pythagoras, similarity) into scope, which is appropriate. Both 0264591c and 6aed5be9 develop 'Steigungswinkel berechnen' in parallel, which is why candidate 6 needs the same edge.

results.rationale: The description asks for the zero of the tangent at the current graph point, which presupposes setting up that tangent from the derivative. f042385e develops exactly this: HMKB KC Mathematik p. 32 has 'Gleichung von Tangente und Normale' in E.2, while Newton's method is in E.6 on p. 34. 0264591c-fdd7-41c6-9fb9-7cb3a03f7658 would also work but adds the slope angle, which is not needed, and b43a1e45 is J10 and applies in only 2 states.
results.concerns: Points backwards within E (E.2 before E.6). The forced drop of the direct edge to 'Ableitung als Steigung im Punkt deuten' is harmless.

results.rationale: An 'Extremwertaufgabe aus Sachsituationen' requires setting up a target function from the context and solving f′(x)=0, usually a linear or quadratic equation; today the goal secures neither modelling with terms nor linear or quadratic equations. a7ccb7a9 is the direct Sek I precursor: it models problems with quadratic functions, interprets extreme values, and secures 'Sachsituationen in Terme mit Variablen übersetzen', linear equations and quadratic equations. The E.1 goal 1b70498a-62a0-5a84-99dd-476b8af68da6 secures the same Sek I base, but it targets choosing a model and fitting parameters rather than optimisation, so it fits less well.
results.concerns: J9 → E points backwards, all 16 states; the goal gains 32 secured goals and 18 later goals grow. A separate gap: the goal does not secure the derivative test for extrema, 350fc8b1-ead0-4239-b28a-217cbd3bd1c3 'Monotonie und Extremstellen mit der ersten Ableitung untersuchen'; 845440ce covers that only graphically.

results.rationale: To get the intersection angle of two graphs from their tangent slopes, the learner turns each slope into an angle (arctan) and compares the angles. The current prerequisite 7c0dee9b-a827-456d-9f88-b196fc4e9a13 does not develop that step. 6aed5be9 is the E sibling that adds exactly the slope angles to the slope competence, so it is the closest fit on this path.
results.concerns: Trigonometry reaches this goal only if candidate 6 is added too; otherwise require 71a483ba directly. The forced removal of the edge from 'Anzahl von Graph-Schnittpunkten anschaulich begründen' to 6aed5be9 is harmless.

results.rationale: 'zugehörige Steigungswinkel berechnen' cannot be met without determining an angle from its tangent in the slope triangle. 71a483ba develops this, and nothing secured for the goal provides it. No narrower Sek I goal on slope angles of lines exists in the listings.
results.concerns: J9 → E points backwards, all 16 states. The edge is identical in substance to candidate 2.

results.rationale: Polynomials up to degree 3 cannot be differentiated term by term without the power, factor and sum rules, yet only the difference-quotient goal is secured today. dde9ae98 develops the factor and sum rule and already secures the power rule e9445479-c188-5c09-842d-faa5e8678099; this matches HMKB KC Mathematik p. 32, E.2 'Ableitungsregeln'. It is narrower than 623cd47f-6f9e-58a7-911c-69e4a8609a27 'Ganzrationale Funktionen ableiten', which would also fit.
results.concerns: Same E.2 path and no cycle. The 236 later goals gain two E.2 goals, which is appropriate, and the forced drop of the direct edge to b42bdfcc is harmless. 858113c5 and 623cd47f both teach differentiating polynomials; consider merging them.

results.rationale: c3c057a3-caf9-44a5-ae60-639e3119e94a (derivatives of e^x and a^x) requires this goal transitively, via 8fa32a68-46eb-414e-8292-a4c4052b2522 and 3a5bf7e5-aacf-4666-b4fa-9868a1e6fcfb. Nothing secured here introduces e or any exponential derivative, so making the later goal a prerequisite would create a cycle. HMKB KC Mathematik E.2 (p. 32) lists only x^n for n ∈ Z, the factor and sum rule and derivatives of polynomials; the derivative of e^x comes in E.4 (p. 33). Drop 'Exponential-', e.g. '… bei ganzrationalen Funktionen bis Grad 3 sowie einfachen Potenzfunktionen mit ganzzahligen Exponenten …'; c3c057a3 keeps the exponential part.
results.concerns: Needs a new description review. Restrict 'Potenzfunktionen' explicitly to integer exponents, because the derivative of √x is developed in Q2 by 6517427b-cf4e-5ebf-9a76-e1035617687c, which also requires this goal. Recheck the later goals that require this goal and may currently rely on it for exponential derivatives (8fa32a68, 628928a6-4f48-54dc-952d-dec0e69dc856).

results.rationale: Reconstructing a polynomial of degree 2–3 from conditions means setting up and solving a linear system with 3–4 unknowns; today not even systems in 2 variables are secured. 5743b8f9 develops exactly this for quadratic functions (3 unknowns, procedure explained as an algorithm) and also secures 546bf0b3-6921-416b-a2ef-8fd37d429dc7. 546bf0b3 alone is narrower but covers only simple systems and is not sufficient.
results.concerns: Scope: 5743b8f9 excludes DE-SH while the goal includes it, so the edge pulls a J9 goal into SH. SH Fachanforderungen Mathematik 2024 (input/SH/Fachanforderungen_Mathematik_Sekundarstufe_2024_barrierearm.pdf) list only 'lineare Gleichungssysteme mit zwei Variablen' in Sek I (p. 38) and put solving linear systems by an algorithm, with the idea of Gauß, in Sek II (p. 61). The content therefore belongs to SH's upper secondary anyway, so I accept the edge, but the clean target would be an SH-applicable Sek II goal for linear systems before E, and the listings have none.

results.rationale: To justify the passage from secant to tangent, the learner must read the difference quotient as the slope Δy/Δx of a straight line. The secured goal ae20183e-92b5-5521-b8e0-9a8662cf51f5 treats it only as a rate in context, and no goal on the slope of a line is secured. 2d75fd3f is the E.1 goal on this path (HMKB E.1 precedes E.2) and it secures the Sek I goal af3d6bff-c5fb-4ec6-a9f0-c0be09fc9186; af3d6bff alone would be an acceptable, narrower alternative.
results.concerns: Points backwards within E. The 263 later goals, including Physics goals, each gain 4 appropriate goals; none of them is a lower-secondary (J-phase) goal.

results.rationale: The clause 'digitale Werkzeuge zur Kontrolle reflektiert einsetzen' cannot be met unless the learner can plot functions with a tool and find zeros and extrema numerically. 1eb7b2ce develops exactly that, and nothing secured provides it. 89ca5089-7122-5a82-b21f-17d0bd46a3bd only plots and varies parameters, and df5eeadd-414e-50ae-84ec-7e5dbf7449d6 is broader (integrals, bisection), so 1eb7b2ce is the best fit.

results.rationale: The exemplary h-method proof for x² and x³ requires expanding (x+h)^n and factoring out h, and no secured goal develops either. e322310f covers both (binomial formulas, transforming and factorising quadratic terms) and secures the J7 transformations by the distributive law needed for (x+h)³. The J8 goal 74dc4b0d-a167-564c-bdc1-5cf510aee280 'Algebraische Terme ausmultiplizieren' is narrower, but it does not cover factoring and is barely connected to the rest of the graph.

If a negative n is expected, adding and subtracting fraction terms would also be needed: 15512e77-31e3-5222-8a6b-84791618e5ce, which excludes DE-SH. The forced removal at 'Erhaltung der mechanischen Energie tiefer verstehen (LK)' is harmless.

results.rationale: Tangent and normal equations are built from a slope and a point, which is the point-slope competence of ae772695; it is not secured today. ae772695 is the only goal in the listings that develops it, and the J10 twin b43a1e45 applies in only 2 states.
results.concerns: J8 → E points backwards, all 16 states. A separate gap: the normal slope −1/m is developed only by the siblings 7c0dee9b and 6aed5be9, which f042385e does not secure.

results.rationale: To determine an instantaneous velocity and read it as a tangent slope in the t-s diagram, the learner uses the instantaneous rate of change as a limit of mean rates. 2143e9e8 develops this and secures the h-method goal b42bdfcc; no secured goal provides it. It is the narrowest fit and continues the existing physics-to-mathematics E link from ce431132 to ae20183e, and both HMKB KCs put this content in E (Physik p. 30, E.1; Mathematik p. 32, E.2).
results.concerns: This is a cross-subject E → E edge with 322 Physics goals that build on it, and it ties Physics E.1 to the timing of Math E.2. Nine SekI-tagged Physics exam tasks already build on this E goal, an existing scope problem, and would take on two more Math E goals. The J10 goal 7156558c-57f1-4372-9ba7-0640c3f7cb3a would point to an earlier phase, but it would break consistency with the E-phase math chain the Physics goals already use.

results.rationale: t-a diagrams presuppose acceleration as Δv/Δt. Only e4b38061-1f28-43ad-8371-a3e7c0e81856 develops it, and e4b38061 transitively requires this goal (via 971beafa and bf8517a9), so making it a prerequisite would create a cycle. Drop 't-a-', giving '… in t-s- und t-v-Diagrammen darstellen und interpretieren'; e4b38061 already covers t-a representations, and HMKB KC Physik p. 30 (E.1) lists 't-s-, t-v- und t-a-Diagramme' and 'Definition der Beschleunigung' in the same topic field, so the source stays covered across the two goals.
results.concerns: Needs a new description review. Velocity for the t-v part is covered only through the mean-rate goal ae20183e ('z. B. Durchschnittsgeschwindigkeit'), which is adequate.

remarks: Main pattern: the E-phase analysis goals secure only grade 5-7 arithmetic; line equations (J8), right-triangle trigonometry (J9), modelling with quadratics, binomial formulas and linear systems are missing. A systematic check of every E-phase entry goal against Sek I would probably find more.
Overlapping goals: four goals in the E tangent cluster (0264591c, f042385e, 6aed5be9, 7c0dee9b) overlap, and 858113c5 overlaps 623cd47f.
Dependency between candidates: candidate 5 gets trigonometry only through candidate 6.

Gaps outside the candidates: f042385e is missing the normal slope; 1511b39a is missing the derivative test for extrema (350fc8b1); nine SekI-tagged Physics exam tasks already require E-phase kinematics.
Forced removals: no problem with either one.
